title: Implement private-first public surfaces for UltraModern apps
description: Implement private-first route publicness and generated public surfaces for app-first UltraModern projects. Normal app screens, auth screens, tenant URLs, dashboards, and internal routes must be private/non-indexable by default. Public surfaces are generated only from explicit public/indexable inputs or generated public starter/docs/help/product routes.
design: Define the smallest route metadata surface: public/indexable flag, title, description, canonical inference, locale awareness, and opt-out behavior. Do not require route owner, id, canonicalPath, or structuredData for normal app screens. Generate robots.txt, sitemap.xml, app manifest, security.txt, optional llms.txt, and API catalog only from safe public inputs. llms.txt and API catalog should be minimal/disabled for private apps unless public docs/help/product/API inputs exist. SEO stability is required: generated public files must be deterministic; sitemap lastmod must change only when page content or metadata changes; if reliable page modification time is unavailable, omit lastmod rather than stamping build time on every deploy. Non-production should noindex/disallow as appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Private/auth/tenant/internal app routes do not appear in robots, sitemap, llms, or API catalogs by default; public routes can opt in with a small metadata API; generated starter public routes may be public by template; sitemap follows indexability and localized public routes; generated outputs are deterministic; sitemap lastmod is stable and not regenerated on every build unless content/metadata changed; no owner/id/canonicalPath/structuredData burden is imposed on app authors; JSON-LD remains deferred.
notes:
Prefactor landed for the first implementation slice: packages/toolkit/create/src/ultramodern-workspace.ts now emits route-owned metadata with public=false, indexable=false, publicSurface=private-app-screen by default, plus a derived publicRoutes list. Generated workspace contracts and integration tests assert that shell/vertical app screens remain private/non-indexable until explicit route metadata opts in. Remaining work: implement robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest, security.txt, optional llms.txt, and API catalog generation from publicRoutes only, with deterministic output and stable/omitted sitemap lastmod.
2026-06-06 subagent validation: keep open. Private-first route metadata/publicRoutes prefactor landed, but generated public artifacts are still missing: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, manifest, security.txt, optional llms.txt, and API catalog generation from publicRoutes only, with deterministic/stable output.
2026-06-06 plan graph saved as modernjs-active-next-work (selection hash 36298c3f13). Exact sequence: ultramodern-opinionated-defaults-02-public-surfaces -> ultramodern-active-01-generated-blockers -> ultramodern-active-02-generated-proof -> ultramodern-active-03-tractor-cleanup. a6d4 resilience/performance work remains deferred outside this active graph.
close_reason: Private-first generated public surfaces implemented and validated: generated workspaces emit disallowing robots.txt by default, omit optional discovery files without safe public routes, record public-surface contract metadata, refresh shell assets during vertical additions, and document the boundary. Gates passed: biome check, @modern-js/create build, create-ultramodern-workspace integration suite, plan-graph validate.

  - modernjs-6mk: missing effect client artifact generation for effect-only data-platform contracts

title: Fix Cloudflare full-stack MicroVertical execution
description:
## Problem
The current generated Cloudflare Worker dynamically imports @modern-js/plugin-bff/effect-edge, but the module is absent from the emitted workerd module graph. Existing acceptance hides this because only the shell runs in workerd while vertical APIs run on Node.

## Steps to Reproduce

The request fails with No such module server/@modern-js/plugin-bff/effect-edge; the current SSR proof harness also rejects ordinary API binding traffic as missing distributed SSR props.

## Required Fix
Fix missing Effect edge runtime modules in generated workerd output, make service-binding proofs handle API requests correctly, and prove SSR plus direct and shell-routed BFF/API behavior inside the actual multi-worker runtime.

title: Fix Node full-stack federation and resilience
description:
## Problem
Node frontend MF/SSR works only when remotes are ready first, while advertised backend-mf-manifest/container URLs return 404 and the backend proof replaces the network entry with file://. Declared shell API prefixes also return 404.

## Steps to Reproduce
Build and serve the generated shell and verticals. Request backend-mf-manifest.json and backendRemoteEntry.mjs from a vertical, call a declared vertical API through the shell prefix, and start the shell before remote manifests are ready. Observe 404s for backend MF/API routes and RUNTIME-003 process failure during shell startup.

## Required Fix
Serve backend MF manifest/container assets through the framework Node server, load them over HTTP in proof, implement the accepted Node API resolution path, and prevent shell process death when remotes are unavailable at startup.
acceptance_criteria: Built Node shell/remotes prove SSR/hydration, backend MF over HTTP, vertical API reachability, startup degraded/recovery behavior, and typed failure without file URL overrides.
notes:
Implemented backend MF infrastructure routing: i18n exemptions, backend MF cache classification, and production assembly coverage for GET/HEAD/OPTIONS/MIME/CORS/cache/localized-404/traversal. Node backend container now emits bundled CommonJS and the official runtime loads it over live HTTP without file://. Architecture correction: production EffectAdapter remains the authoritative compiled API executable; one immutable Node envelope now binds actual compiled api/**/*.js plus shared/**/*.js as apiBackend and binds backend-mf-manifest.json/backendRemoteEntry.cjs separately. Envelope plugin declares pre dependencies on plugin-bff and backend-federation build so both final artifacts exist before hashing; actual plugin-manager ordering regression passes. Server serves backend manifest/container byte-exact so live SHA can equal envelope (no dynamic publicPath mutation). Generated Node proof now requires/fetches live manifest and container, matches URL/path/byteLength/SHA to envelope, calls live readiness API, and matches response marker to envelope identity/apiBackend artifacts. Focused tests/builds green. Remaining blocker before close: fresh generated runtime/network proof and removal of obsolete post-build backend generator step, which currently overwrites Cloudflare backend-mf-manifest.json after envelope emission (expected 2876 bytes dd4e..., overwritten 2515 bytes 7c53...), correctly causing deploy verification to fail.
Fresh current-source compiler audit (2026-07-18): source-linked generated workspace previously entered monorepo node_modules during plugin-bff compileApi TS-Go and failed on four unpatched MF/Effect declaration errors. Workspace-source linking now uses workspace-wide pnpm injection/linking; focused tests 16/16, integration/content/tooling/version 52/52, create and plugin-bff builds, and targeted Biome all pass. Controlled fresh fixture reaches TS-Go compile succeed on Node. Per-app build no longer redundantly regenerates backend MF after modern build; explicit root repair/proof command remains. Current next Node blocker belongs to release-envelope collection: no compiled API/backend module carries exact final buildMarker/sourceRevision/releaseVersion. Log: /tmp/modernjs-plugin-bff-generated-fixed-node-build.log. Issue remains open.

title: Add UltraModern resilience i18n and performance readiness gates
description: Add UltraModern resilience/status defaults, localized public metadata, and cautious optional performance-readiness gates. This must cover both Effect BFF/server behavior and React/frontend runtime behavior. Accessibility certification is explicitly removed from this roadmap.
design: BFF/Effect side: correct 500/503 behavior, typed failure envelopes where owned, maintenance mode with Retry-After, production stack leak prevention, upstream timeout/degradation behavior, operation context, and telemetry. React/FE side: correct route-level 404/500 boundaries, deterministic Module Federation remote fallback, no trust bypass during fallback, user-visible degraded states where framework-owned, and telemetry for fallback/recovery. Localized metadata/hreflang applies only to public/indexable routes and must not expose private app screens. Optional performance-readiness checks may cover navigation warmup waste ratio, duplicate prefetches, Save-Data behavior, cache policy sanity, BFCache diagnostics, Core Web Vitals/RUM readiness, and Cloudflare SSR response/caching hints. These checks are diagnostics or opt-in release gates, not default build blockers.
acceptance_criteria: 404/500/503 statuses are correct across relevant server/runtime paths; production stack leaks are avoided; maintenance Retry-After is supported where owned; Effect BFF failures and React FE route/fallback failures have deterministic behavior and telemetry; MF fallback preserves trust, compatibility, and telemetry contracts; localized metadata/hreflang is generated only for public routes; performance-readiness gates are optional diagnostics/opt-in release gates; accessibility certification is absent; docs explain defaults versus optional readiness.
notes:
Defaults contract now lives in docs/super-app-rfc-adr/ADR-0016-ultramodern-opinionated-defaults-contract.md. No resilience/performance runtime implementation landed in this slice. Remaining work should keep resilience in server/runtime/BFF owners and performance-readiness as diagnostics or opt-in gates; accessibility certification remains out of scope.
2026-06-06 subagent validation: keep open. Adjacent warmup/security/public-route slices landed elsewhere, but core resilience/performance readiness is not implemented: production-safe BFF/runtime failure envelopes, maintenance Retry-After, 503 behavior, stack/message redaction, deterministic FE/MF degraded behavior with telemetry, and optional BFCache/Core Web Vitals/RUM/cache diagnostics remain.
2026-06-06 deeper subagent validation: moved from in_progress broad implementation issue to open parent/meta tracker. Split executable work into children: modernjs-a6d4.3 BFF/server resilience, modernjs-a6d4.1 frontend route error hardening, modernjs-a6d4.4 MF degraded-state telemetry, and modernjs-a6d4.2 opt-in performance diagnostics. Localized public metadata belongs under modernjs-04jb, not this parent.
2026-06-06 owner direction: deprioritize the resilience/performance split for now; come back to modernjs-a6d4 children after public surfaces, generated variant validation, and Tractor cleanup are handled.
close_reason: All executable resilience/performance children are complete: server/BFF resilience, frontend route error hardening including deferred/RSC redaction, default-on opt-out performance diagnostics, and MF degraded-state telemetry. Accessibility certification and mixed-bundler MF are intentionally out of scope.

comments.author: UltraModern Debug
comments.text:
Reachability audit refreshed 2026-07-27 against fork default branch main-ultramodern (alerts ARE current, not stale upstream state): 56 open = 17 high / 34 moderate / 5 low.

Dominant noise source: 36 of 56 alerts (5 of them high, all hono) come from tests/skill/fixtures/real-v2-bff-hono/package.json, which declares 'hono': '^3.12.2'. The workspace lock resolves hono@4.12.28, already above every advisory fix version (4.10.2/4.11.4/4.12.4/4.12.25). Not shipped, not built into any package. Bumping the fixture's declared range clears 36 alerts at zero runtime risk.

Genuine runtime finding, highest priority: react-router is a hard-pinned production dependency '8.1.0' of the SHIPPED package packages/toolkit/runtime-utils; advisory range >=7.12.0 <8.3.0, fix 8.3.0.

Remaining high findings resolve via pnpm-lock.yaml (installed -> fix): adm-zip 0.5.10 -> 0.6.0; axios 1.16.1 -> 1.18.0 (1.18.1 also present); fast-uri 4.1.0 -> 4.1.1; js-yaml 3.14.2 -> 3.15.0 and 5.2.1 -> 5.2.2 (also declared in scripts/prebundle); postcss 8.5.16 -> 8.5.18; sharp 0.34.5 -> 0.35.0 (0.35.3 also present); svgo 4.0.0/4.0.1 -> 4.0.2.

Conclusion: the '56 vulnerabilities' headline is mostly one stale test fixture. Actionable set is far smaller, and only react-router touches a published package.

title: Fix Cloudflare Worker SSR route dispatch before asset fallback

This was observed on the public Tractor deployment after publishing 3.5.0-ultramodern.14: /en and federated routes returned
with no SSR markers and only shell CSS, even though the generated route manifest marks the route as isSSR and local SSR proof passes. Fix the owning Modern.js Cloudflare wrapper/generator so SSR document routes dispatch to the route worker before static asset fallback, while preserving real asset serving and fast asset-miss behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Cloudflare Worker wrapper tests prove SSR document routes run the route worker before assets SPA fallback; static assets are still served by assets binding; asset-like misses do not SSR; Tractor migrates to the fixed cohort and public Workers proof includes SSR markers and remote CSS links.
close_reason: Fixed in Modern.js commits 42e1e942f0 and bdf3da3cac, published as 3.5.0-ultramodern.17. Validation: @modern-js/runtime tests/build passed; Tractor migrated to .17, pnpm check/build/cloudflare:build passed, Workers redeployed, cloudflare-proof and workflow proof passed, raw public HTML includes non-empty SSR root markup, MF boundary markers, translated head metadata, and remote CSS links.

design: Single source of truth for release cohort and a single acceptance runner. Publish consumes already accepted artifacts without semantic rebuild. Shared workflow/config files remain main-thread owned; parallel agents begin read-only and later writers receive disjoint scopes.
acceptance_criteria: Before any new npm version: exact publish artifacts are built once and hashed; a clean generated erp-10 workspace installs those artifacts and passes format, lint, typecheck, contracts, build, and required runtime proofs; release-age exclusions are derived from canonical cohort data; post-publish readiness reuses the same runner and becomes verification; regression tests cover every .37-.44 failure class. After trusted publish to bleedingdev only, post-publish readiness passes and Tractor is migrated, fully validated, committed, and pushed.
notes: 2026-07-10 resumed release audit: exact detached acceptance found the release builder replaying 30/30 Nx tasks from cache because NX_SKIP_NX_CACHE=1 was ineffective. Commits 05cb7f903b and dec169404b now force documented local/remote cache bypass flags and gate that argv in Workflow Security; test:scripts is 160/160 and .45 remains absent across all 32 npm packages with latest still .44. Release remains paused before prepare/pack because the Tractor audit proved current generator output still emits forbidden app-level Zephyr fail-open/disable behavior, diagnostics suppressions, MF/TanStack workaround flags/loaders, and hard window.location.assign navigation. Owning-layer repair graph is active; Tractor's 17 dirty .44 migration files remain untouched.

title: Investigate UltraModern i18n checker AST rule proposal
description: Confirm where the generated i18n checker is owned, why the regex scanner can produce TypeScript generic false positives, and whether an Oxlint JS plugin is a suitable replacement for the UltraModern generated contract.
acceptance_criteria: Evidence-backed confirmation of current wiring, root cause, Oxlint feasibility, affected files, and recommended next implementation path.
notes: Confirmed. Current generated checker lives at packages/toolkit/create/template/scripts/check-i18n-strings.mjs and uses raw regex for visible attributes and >...< JSX text. Reproduced false positives with TypeScript/Effect generic code in an isolated .tsx fixture: the regex reports fragments like '= Effect.Effect' and '(effect: AppEffect'. package.json.handlebars wires i18n:check to node ./scripts/check-i18n-strings.mjs, validate-ultramodern requires the file and exact script, and ultramodern:check includes pnpm i18n:check. Official Oxlint docs confirm JS plugins via jsPlugins and ESLint-compatible AST traversal/rule options, but JS plugins are alpha/not semver-stable. Isolated oxlint@1.68.0 test confirmed JSXText/JSXAttribute visitors report actual hardcoded JSX copy and ignore TS generic syntax. Recommended implementation: keep scripts/check-i18n-strings.mjs as the generated contract wrapper, add a dedicated scripts/i18n Oxlint JS plugin plus JSON config, invoke oxlint src with -A all and the custom rule enabled, and handle subproject output because --sub currently removes oxlint/oxfmt/ultracite while retaining i18n:check.
close_reason: Investigation confirmed and follow-up implementation filed as modernjs-9rcl.

title: Define shared routes and HTTP data outcomes
description:
Define neutral filesystem route IR for nested/layout/pathless/dynamic/dotted/optional/splat routes and data/loading/error/search metadata. Native adapters own matching, parameter extraction, loading/preloading, invalidation, cancellation and navigation via public native TanStack APIs. Shared orchestration invokes a per-request native router factory and normalizes HTTP/data results; remove any dependency on React Router static handlers in shared paths. Specify loader/action request/context input, redirect/not-found/error/success outcomes, repeated headers/cookies, rich-value serialization and revalidation. Decide HTTP outcomes and cache intent before rendering. Isolate native route types/module augmentations; do not impose one router-core version across unproved adapters. Serialization excludes view values, arbitrary functions and request-owned secrets.
Generated UltraModern apps adopt TanStack route semantics while upstream React Router applications retain their existing path. Characterize current React data/action behavior first; do not replace its executor merely to simplify abstraction. A shared server-only data protocol executes router-selected work; native router hooks own scheduling/preload/cache/cancel/revalidation. Specify framework-owned native action/form bindings explicitly, since TanStack Router has no automatic forms/actions. No server loader code is bundled into clients.

Do not invent a general executable codec; prove admitted rich values, malformed/error/schema handling and safe HTML/script framing under CSP without blanket unsafe-eval. Ordinary loader-data codec is separate from Octane signals and native lazy-module hydration.
Gate closure uses standalone infrastructure/admission-host protocol fixtures. description:
